 nanobot

🐈 nanobot is a lightweight, open-source, self-hosted personal AI agent written in Python. Chat with it from your browser, terminal, or favorite chat app to work with files, remember preferences, use tools, and run scheduled tasks—powered by any supported cloud or local AI model.

 💡 Why nanobot

- Lightweight & low footprint: Small Python core with fast startup and low memory usage—runs comfortably on a personal laptop or a modest VPS without heavyweight infrastructure.
- Polished WebUI & native TUI out of the box: Includes a clean, responsive browser workbench (multi-pane topics, live tool activity, inline file diffs, context usage, themes, and custom backgrounds) plus a matching terminal UI—no separate frontend build needed.
- Works where you already chat: Connect seamlessly to 15+ chat apps including Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, WeChat, WhatsApp, Email, Mattermost, and Linear.
- Real tools, memory & automations: Reads images, PDFs, and Office files ( .docx , .xlsx , .pptx ), edits files, connects to MCP servers and plugins, builds long-term memory with Dream, and runs scheduled tasks, local triggers, and sustained goals.
- Model freedom & full control: Use any cloud API (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek), OAuth subscription (OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, xAI Grok), or local server (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio)—self-hosted on your own machine.

 🚀 Quick Start

If the installer already opened the WebUI in your browser, continue right there. Otherwise run:

 

 Your first three steps: 

1. Open Settings → Models , create a preset, and add your provider API key (or sign in with OAuth). See Configure Your Model.
2. Start a new topic and send Hello! to verify your model connection.
3. Try a file task: pick a practice folder with Restricted access and ask "Read notes.txt and write a short summary to summary.md." See Your first file task.

Once that works, you can ask nanobot right in chat to help configure your next feature—for example: "I am using the WebUI. Help me connect Telegram and allow only my account." (See Continue with nanobot.)

install.html:
Requires Python 3.11 or newer and an account on a supported AI provider or local model server. Packaged installs include both the WebUI and terminal UI—no frontend build tools required.

[!NOTE] This README tracks the latest development branch; the installer below installs the latest stable release. For published release docs, visit nanobot.wiki.

Recommended: one-command installer (installs into an isolated environment and opens the WebUI automatically on desktop)

macOS / Linux

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

Windows PowerShell

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
Preview the installer or inspect the scripts first

Preview what the installer will do without changing anything:

# macOS / Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run

# Windows PowerShell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HKUDS/nanobot/main/scripts/install.ps1))) --dry-run

Or read scripts/install.sh and scripts/install.ps1 directly.

Other install methods: uv, pip, or from source

uv

uv tool install nanobot-ai
nanobot webui

pip (inside a virtual environment)

python -m pip install nanobot-ai
nanobot webui

From source (latest main, requires Git)

git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot.git
cd nanobot
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e .
nanobot webui

For full install options, troubleshooting nanobot: command not found, or updating an existing install, see Install and Quick Start and Updating nanobot.
